title: Tracking Diseases Cured by AI
lede: A single-page tracker counts diseases cured with AI's help, following the AI-derived drug candidates nearest approval and separating treatments from cures.

points: Insilico Medicine's rentosertib for idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis leads: AI chose both its target and molecule, and a 320-patient Phase III began in 2026.
Takeda and Nimbus's zasocitinib for psoriasis has an FDA decision due in Q1 2027, though the site notes it came from older physics-based modelling of a known target.
Isomorphic Labs raised $2.1B in May 2026 but had dosed no molecule in a human by November.
The site counts managing a disease, as with psoriasis, as distinct from curing it.

points.text: A commenter who works in the field says AI does speed up science, but measuring what happens inside cells, not crunching data, is the real bottleneck.
Several ask how many diseases medicine has ever cured, with antibiotics and a hepatitis C drug offered as examples.
Readers split on whether this is serious tracking or a sneer, since it gives AI no credit for partial progress.
One commenter finds the tone bitter, reading it as assuming that what has not happened yet will not happen.
